sections.html:
Auburn has 86,301 residents (July 1, 2025). About 60.6% of homes are owner-occupied, households average 2.79 people, and owner-occupied homes were worth a median $547,900 across 2020 to 2024. Median household income was $97,884 and the average commute was 30.5 minutes. Most of Auburn lies in King County. A sliver reaches into Pierce County, and that decides who sends your tax bill.

Auburn grew by annexation. In 2008 it took in the West Hill and Lea Hill areas of unincorporated King County, about 15,000 residents, and on January 1, 2024 it added the 155-acre Bridges neighborhood from Kent. Lakeland Hills, the master-planned community southeast of downtown, is split between King and Pierce counties.

sections.h2: Is the address really inside Auburn?
sections.html: An "Auburn" mailing address does not always mean the City of Auburn. Some addresses that carry the name belong to King County, Kent or Federal Way. Before you assume city permit and rental rules apply, run the property through the city's interactive map. A wrong guess can send you to the wrong office for permits and change which tax bill you pay.

Most of the city is in the Auburn School District, which also serves Algona, Pacific and some unincorporated areas. Parts of north Auburn are in the Federal Way and Kent districts, and the Pierce County portion falls in the Dieringer School District. District lines follow streets, so look up your own address before listing. Buyers with children ask first, and the answer can differ between two houses on the same road. Put the district name in your listing notes so nobody has to guess.

State Route 167 (the Valley Freeway) and State Route 18 run through town. Sounder trains from Auburn station reach downtown Seattle in about 30 minutes, Sound Transit buses connect to Federal Way, Sumner and Kent, and King County Metro buses serve Auburn Way and Green River College. Highlight the commute options in your listing, since many Auburn buyers work elsewhere in the valley or in Seattle.

sections.h2: Do I need a rental license in Auburn?
sections.html:
For most rentals, yes. Auburn requires an owner to hold a Rental Housing License for most forms of renting residential property, so the city has current ownership and management details for homes the owner does not live in. Selling a house with tenants in it? Check that the license is current first. Rental license rules are in Auburn City Code 5.22, and the Permit Center answers questions at 253-931-3090, option 2.

Rental typeCity requirement
Owner-occupied home, renting rooms to 2 or fewer peopleCity business license not required; occupancy limit is family plus 2.
Owner-occupied home, renting rooms to more than 2 peopleCity business license required; occupancy limit is family plus 4.
Non-owner-occupied home, one lease for the entire homeCity business license required; no inspection.
Non-owner-occupied home, more than one lease (communal residence)License required; occupancy limit of 4; initial inspection before issuance and annual inspection before renewal.
ApartmentsCity business license required; no inspection.

Auburn takes permit applications online through MyBuildingPermit.com. Electrical permits inside city limits come from the Washington Department of Labor and Industries. A house on a septic system needs approval from the King County or Pierce County health department for most changes. If you built a deck, finished a basement or changed wiring, find out now whether a permit exists, because buyers and inspectors ask.

Washington also hands you a form to complete. Under RCW 64.06.020 you complete a disclosure statement on the property and deliver it after both sides sign a written contract. The deadline is five business days from mutual acceptance. Two exceptions exist: the buyer waived the form, or the transfer is exempt. Once the buyer has it, a three-business-day window opens in which the buyer may rescind. The form opens with questions on title and water, so pull your records together before you list.

King County parcels are billed by the King County treasurer. Pierce County parcels go through the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer, (253) 798-6111. The two installments fall on April 30 and October 31 (RCW 84.56.020). The lien starts January 1. Absent a contract term, RCW 84.60.020 assigns each of you the days you owned the house, and escrow runs the numbers at closing.

The seller generally pays the state's excise tax on the transfer, remitted to the county treasurer on the day of sale. Under the schedule for sales starting January 1, 2027, price up to $551,000 is taxed at 1.1%, price between that and $1,551,000 at 1.28%, and anything above at higher rates. Auburn's median value of $547,900 sits just under the first bracket, so a typical sale there would pay the lowest state rate plus the local share. Your closing agent can confirm the local rate and any exemption.

RCW 84.36.381 offers a property tax exemption to owners who are 61 or older, to certain disabled owners, and to some who served in the military. If you sell, the status can follow you to a replacement home. The county assessor has the current income limits.

sections.h2: What to have ready for escrow
sections.html: Gather these before you accept an offer: your latest tax statement from whichever county bills you, any permit records for decks, basement work or wiring, the rental license if tenants live in the house, and the completed disclosure form. If the house is on a septic system, add the health department approvals. A buyer who sees complete records tends to move faster, and escrow can answer payoff questions without chasing you for papers. If anything is missing, the Permit Center line above is the first call for city records, and the county treasurer is the call for tax balances.

Step one is checking which county and which school district the house falls in. Step two is gathering permit records, rental license paperwork if tenants live there, and your latest tax statement. Step three is completing the disclosure form and handing it over within the five-business-day window. Escrow then orders title work, prorates taxes and settles any unpaid balance from your proceeds. With a cash purchase there is no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait on, so timing rests on title work and how fast your own paperwork is ready.

faqs.q: Which county bills my Auburn property tax?
faqs.a: Most Auburn parcels are in King County and are billed by the King County treasurer. Homes in the Pierce County portion, including part of Lakeland Hills, are billed by the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer.

faqs.q: Does my Auburn mailing address mean I am inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. Some addresses that include Auburn fall under King County, Kent or Federal Way. Use the city's interactive map before assuming city permit and rental rules apply.

faqs.q: Do I need a city license to rent rooms in my Auburn home?
faqs.a: You need a City of Auburn business license if you rent rooms to more than two people. Renting to two or fewer people in an owner-occupied home does not require one, and the occupancy limit is family plus 2.

faqs.q: How soon does the buyer get my disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Five business days from the moment both sides accept the written contract. The form can be skipped if the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt, and the buyer gets three business days after delivery to rescind.

faqs.q: What state transfer tax rate would apply to a typical Auburn sale?
faqs.a: The first bracket for sales starting January 1, 2027 is 1.1% up to $551,000, and Auburn's $547,900 median value sits inside it. A local rate comes on top.
